title: kernel: a failed boot's rollbackStartedPlugins() destroys only plugins whose start() succeeded, while performShutdown() destroys every plugin with a destroy — a plugin that initialised but did not start is never torn down on a refused boot
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbdHk3orAeensH6EzS

Filing gate: ① · Source: fleet (L1 S3 of seat repo:objectstack#5 on PR #37450, comment 7184319598; contract record 7184310941; the #37429 dev's out-of-scope note). Follow-up of #37429.

Grading: `area:data` · reach: read — `packages/core/src/kernel.ts` `rollbackStartedPlugins()` (called at ~:587 and ~:671 on a failed boot) destroys only plugins whose `start()` succeeded; `performShutdown()` destroys every plugin that has a `destroy`. A plugin whose `init()` opened a resource and whose `start()` never ran (or failed) keeps it after a refused boot · evidence: read, no measured wrong answer (on #37429 the datasource-admin plugin's destroy happened to close the default datasource).
Suggested-grade: p3 · resource left open after a refused boot in-process (tests, embedded hosts); a process exit cleans it.

## What

Decide one teardown rule for both paths: on a failed boot, destroy every plugin whose `init()` ran (in reverse order), as shutdown does, or record why rollback is narrower. Pin it with a plugin that opens a resource in `init()` and a boot that fails before or during its `start()`.

Related: #37429 (PR #37450).
Dedupe: searched 'rollbackStartedPlugins' — no open card.
